Work only from the inputs named above.","status":"completed","executionSteps":[{"id":"dispatch","label":"Queued for execution","status":"completed","at":"2026-11-16T17:00:12.364Z"},{"id":"zeus-runtime","label":"Run Agent runtime","status":"completed","at":"2026-11-16T17:00:12.364Z"},{"id":"complete","label":"Finish and record result","status":"completed","at":"2026-11-16T17:00:12.364Z"}],"createdAt":"2026-11-16T17:00:05.642Z","agentWallet":"0x5362d31881716ce4921455bfa8052ae25f4da7d6","model":"advanced","schedule":{"type":"once","runAtMs":1794848405642},"runAtMs":1794848405642,"result":{"response":"**Three methods** (Section 2, "Authenticated Requests"): "This section defines three methods of sending bearer access tokens in resource requests to resource servers. Clients MUST NOT use more than one method to transmit the token in each request."

**1. Authorization request header field** (Section 2.1) — `Authorization: Bearer mF_9.B5f-4.1JqM`

**2. Form-encoded body parameter** (Section 2.2) — `access_token` in an `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body, on a method whose body has defined semantics (so never GET).

**3. URI query parameter** (Section 2.3) — `GET /resource?access_token=mF_9.B5f-4.1JqM`

**What resource servers MUST support: the Authorization header.** Section 2.1: "Clients SHOULD make authenticated requests with a bearer token using the "Authorization" request header field with the "Bearer" HTTP authorization scheme. Resource servers MUST support this method." The other two are optional for servers — "Resource servers MAY support this method" appears in both 2.2 and 2.3.

**What SHOULD NOT be used: the URI query parameter.** Section 2.3: "Because of the security weaknesses associated with the URI method (see Section 5), including the high likelihood that the URL containing the access token will be logged, it SHOULD NOT be used unless it is impossible to transport the access token in the "Authorization" request header field or the HTTP request entity-body." The RFC adds: "This method is included to document current use; its use is not recommended, due to its security deficiencies (see Section 5) and also because it uses a reserved query parameter name, which is counter to URI namespace best practices."

Section 5.3 gives the underlying reason: "Browsers, web servers, and other software may not adequately secure URLs in the browser history, web server logs, and other data structures. If bearer tokens are passed in page URLs, attackers might be able to steal them from the history data, logs, or other unsecured locations."

One related caveat, since it's the same question one level down: the body method also carries a SHOULD NOT, narrower in scope. Section 2.2: "The "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" method SHOULD NOT be used except in application contexts where participating browsers do not have access to the "Authorization" request header field."
